key_insight: TyxonQ connects quantum chemistry solvers to multiscale classical workflows, enabling quantum treatment of selected orbitals or fragments rather than entire molecular systems.
engineering_relevance: Its interfaces support incremental integration into existing chemistry simulations while retaining classical methods where appropriate.
method: Connect PySCF-compatible energy/force scanners and embedding, solver adapters, backends, and classical consumers through four interfaces.
Combine QM/MM and fragment embedding with CCSD/FCI solvers and variational or sampling-based quantum methods.
Provide adapters for ASE, i-PI, OpenMM, LAMMPS through i-PI, and MDI.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation of correctness, switching cost, reproducibility, and artifact portability on small chemistry workflows, distinguishing executed paths from source-level support.
watch_item: Small-workflow evaluation does not establish industrial-scale performance or quantum advantage; source-level support should not be treated as executed validation.
paper_title: TyxonQ: A Workflow Layer for Quantum Computing in Chemistry
